# Information Security Standard: System and Information Integrity

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This standard establishes requirements for system and information integrity controls at Acme Health. All organizational systems and system components must comply with the requirements specified herein.

## 2. Malicious Code Protection

### 2.1 Implementation Requirements

The organization shall implement signature-based or non-signature-based malicious code protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points to detect and eradicate malicious code. [NIST 800-53 SI-3 Low, Moderate, High]

The organization shall implement both signature-based and non-signature-based malicious code protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points to detect and eradicate malicious code. [ARC-AMPE SI-3 AE Mandatory]

### 2.2 Update Requirements

The organization shall automatically update malicious code protection mechanisms as new releases are available in accordance with organizational configuration management policy and procedures. [NIST 800-53 SI-3 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SI-3 AE Mandatory]

The organization shall update malicious code protection mechanisms only when directed by a privileged user. [NIST 800-53 SI-3(4)]

### 2.3 Scanning Configuration

The organization shall configure malicious code protection mechanisms to perform periodic scans of the system [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and real-time scans of files from external sources at [Selection (one or more): endpoint; network entry and exit points] as the files are downloaded, opened, or executed in accordance with organizational policy. [NIST 800-53 SI-3 Low, Moderate, High]

The organization shall configure malicious code protection mechanisms to perform periodic scans of the system at least every one (1) week and real-time scans of files from external sources at endpoints and network entry and exit points as the files are downloaded, opened, or executed in accordance with organizational policy. [ARC-AMPE SI-3 AE Mandatory]

### 2.4 Response to Detection

The organization shall configure malicious code protection mechanisms to [Selection (one or more): block malicious code; quarantine malicious code; take [Assignment: organization-defined action]] and send alert to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] in response to malicious code detection. [NIST 800-53 SI-3 Low, Moderate, High]

The organization shall configure malicious code protection mechanisms to block and quarantine malicious code and send alert to administrator or organization-defined security personnel near real-time in response to malicious code detection. [ARC-AMPE SI-3 AE Mandatory]

### 2.5 False Positive Management

The organization shall address the receipt of false positives during malicious code detection and eradication and the resulting potential impact on the availability of the system. [NIST 800-53 SI-3 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SI-3 AE Mandatory]

### 2.6 Reporting

The organization shall report malicious code scanning results to organization personnel responsible for Incident Handling in compliance with IR-4 and for Audit Review, Analysis, and Reporting in compliance with AU-6. [ARC-AMPE SI-3 AE Mandatory]

### 2.7 Testing

The organization shall test malicious code protection mechanisms [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] by introducing known benign code into the system and verify that the detection of the code and the associated incident reporting occur. [NIST 800-53 SI-3(6)]

### 2.8 Unauthorized Command Detection

The organization shall detect [Assignment: organization-defined unauthorized operating system commands] through the kernel application programming interface on [Assignment: organization-defined system hardware components] and [Selection (one or more): issue a warning; audit the command execution; prevent the execution of the command]. [NIST 800-53 SI-3(8)]

### 2.9 Malicious Code Analysis

The organization shall employ [Assignment: organization-defined tools and techniques] to analyze the characteristics and behavior of malicious code and incorporate the results from malicious code analysis into organizational incident response and flaw remediation processes. [NIST 800-53 SI-3(10)]

## 3. Security and Privacy Function Verification

### 3.1 Verification Requirements

The organization shall verify the correct operation of [Assignment: organization-defined security and privacy functions]. [NIST 800-53 SI-6 High | ARC-AMPE SI-6 AE Mandatory]

### 3.2 Verification Timing

The organization shall perform the verification of security and privacy functions [Selection (one or more): [Assignment: organization-defined system transitional states]; upon command by user with appropriate privilege; [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]]. [NIST 800-53 SI-6 High]

The organization shall perform the verification of security and privacy functions upon system startup and/or restart, upon command by a user with appropriate privileges, or at least monthly. [ARC-AMPE SI-6 AE Mandatory]

### 3.3 Failure Alerting

The organization shall alert [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] to failed security and privacy verification tests. [NIST 800-53 SI-6 High]

The organization shall alert, at a minimum, the system/security administrator to failed security and privacy verification tests. [ARC-AMPE SI-6 AE Mandatory]

### 3.4 Anomaly Response

The organization shall [Selection (one or more): shut the system down; restart the system; [Assignment: organization-defined alternative action(s)]] when anomalies are discovered. [NIST 800-53 SI-6 High]

The organization shall shut the system down, restart the system, or perform another defined alternative action(s) documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP) when anomalies are discovered. [ARC-AMPE SI-6 AE Mandatory]

### 3.5 Distributed Testing Management

The organization shall implement automated mechanisms to support the management of distributed security and privacy function testing. [NIST 800-53 SI-6(2)]

### 3.6 Verification Reporting

The organization shall report the results of security and privacy function verification to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]. [NIST 800-53 SI-6(3)]

## 4. Spam Protection

### 4.1 Implementation Requirements

The organization shall employ spam protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points to detect and act on unsolicited messages. [NIST 800-53 SI-8 Moderate, High | FedRAMP SI-8 | ARC-AMPE SI-8 AE Mandatory]

### 4.2 Update Requirements

The organization shall update spam protection mechanisms when new releases are available in accordance with organizational configuration management policy and procedures. [NIST 800-53 SI-8 Moderate, High | FedRAMP SI-8 | ARC-AMPE SI-8 AE Mandatory]

The organization shall automatically update spam protection mechanisms [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]. [NIST 800-53 SI-8(2) Moderate, High]

The organization shall automatically update spam protection mechanisms at least every one (1) week. [ARC-AMPE SI-8(2) AE Mandatory]

### 4.3 DMARC Requirements

When CSO sends email on behalf of the government as part of the business offering, the organization shall implement Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting & Conformance (DMARC) on the sending domain for outgoing messages as described in DHS Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 18-01, confirming DMARC configuration with policy=reject and the rua parameter includes reports@dmarc.cyber.dhs.gov, and documenting DMARC compliance in the SI-08 control implementation solution description including the FROM: domain(s) when emails are sent on behalf of the government. [FedRAMP SI-8]

### 4.4 Learning Capability

The organization shall implement spam protection mechanisms with a learning capability to more effectively identify legitimate communications traffic. [NIST 800-53 SI-8(3)]

## 5. Memory Protection

The organization shall implement [Assignment: organization-defined controls] to protect the system memory from unauthorized code execution. [NIST 800-53 SI-16 Moderate, High]

The organization shall implement, at a minimum, the related controls within this control set to protect the system memory from unauthorized code execution. [ARC-AMPE SI-16 AE Mandatory]

## 6. Portable Media Control

### 6.1 Media Use Restrictions

The organization shall [Selection: restrict; prohibit] the use of [Assignment: organization-defined types of system media] on [Assignment: organization-defined systems or system components] using [Assignment: organization-defined controls]. [NIST 800-53 MP-7 Low, Moderate, High]

The organization shall prohibit the use of personally owned media (e.g., flash drives, external hard disk drives, and other portable storage and media devices) on organization-defined systems and networks using organization-defined security safeguards. [ARC-AMPE MP-7 AE Mandatory]

### 6.2 Unidentifiable Media

The organization shall prohibit the use of portable storage devices in organizational systems when such devices have no identifiable owner. [NIST 800-53 MP-7 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE MP-7 AE Mandatory]

### 6.3 Sanitization-Resistant Media

The organization shall prohibit the use of sanitization-resistant media in organizational systems. [NIST 800-53 MP-7(2)]

## 7. Mobile Code

### 7.1 Mobile Code Definition

The organization shall define acceptable and unacceptable mobile code and mobile code technologies. [NIST 800-53 SC-18 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SC-18 AE Mandatory]

The organization shall define the acceptable and unacceptable mobile code and mobile code technologies in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP). [ARC-AMPE SC-18 AE Mandatory]

### 7.2 Mobile Code Management

The organization shall authorize, monitor, and control the use of mobile code within the system. [NIST 800-53 SC-18 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SC-18 AE Mandatory]

### 7.3 Unacceptable Mobile Code Handling

The organization shall identify [Assignment: organization-defined unacceptable mobile code] and take [Assignment: organization-defined corrective actions]. [NIST 800-53 SC-18(1)]

The organization shall prevent the download and execution of [Assignment: organization-defined unacceptable mobile code]. [NIST 800-53 SC-18(3)]

### 7.4 Mobile Code Acquisition and Development

The organization shall verify that the acquisition, development, and use of mobile code to be deployed in the system meets [Assignment: organization-defined mobile code requirements]. [NIST 800-53 SC-18(2)]

### 7.5 Mobile Code Execution Controls

The organization shall prevent the automatic execution of mobile code in [Assignment: organization-defined software applications] and enforce [Assignment: organization-defined actions] prior to executing the code. [NIST 800-53 SC-18(4)]

The organization shall allow execution of permitted mobile code only in confined virtual machine environments. [NIST 800-53 SC-18(5)]
